answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted attestations: a review counts only if its author has locked collateral, and peers slash that deposit when one node poses as many. An attacker could spin up polished personas named opal, sable, and terrace, but each needs its own bond, so influence costs real capital instead of a few spare cycles. The attack price is the sum of every locked stake plus all of it forfeited once the deception is proven. Fake identities cannot climb a trust ladder whose rungs are all paid for.
